title: Security changes, round 3: reuse what the app already has

steps.path: When the assistant tries to send a form on a website
steps.headline: The send-a-form question now sits in the same frosted card as the chat's other permission questions.
steps.changed: It is now drawn by the chat's own permission card, inside the same frosted bubble. The old one sat directly on the chat, so the wallpaper showed through.
steps.notice: Same look, same Yes / Always allow / No buttons, and Enter works like it does on every other question.
steps.risk: Yes is one form; Always allow remembers the site, as before.

steps.path: When the assistant first uses a site
steps.headline: The website question uses the same card: Yes, Always allow, No.
steps.changed: Replaces Not now / Always allow / Allow for this chat. Yes now means for this chat.
steps.notice: The three buttons match every other question.
steps.risk: Always allow still remembers the site.

steps.path: When the assistant is about to click a step that buys or sends
steps.headline: The last-step question (buying, sending, deleting) uses the same card: Yes or No.
steps.changed: Replaces Don't allow / Allow this once. Yes allows this one step only.
steps.notice: Same card. There is no Always allow here, as before.
steps.risk: Enter does not answer this one, only a click, so a stray key can never buy something.

steps.path: When the assistant wants an address on your home network
steps.headline: The home-network question uses the same card: Yes or No.
steps.changed: Replaces Don't allow / Allow for this chat. Yes covers this chat.

steps.headline: The Account page loses the Sign out everywhere row.
steps.changed: "Lost a device?" and its button are gone from this page.
steps.notice: A quieter page. Sign out everywhere moved one level down, next to Delete account.
steps.risk: It is one press further away (Edit account, then scroll down).

steps.headline: Sign out everywhere now works like Delete account: a red button, then a red note with Cancel and the action.
steps.changed: It sits in the Danger zone on Edit account. Pressing it shows one note: "Ends your YouCoded sign-in on every device, this one too. Phones paired for remote access stay paired."
steps.notice: Same two-step as deleting an account, without the typed word, since signing in again undoes it.
steps.risk: If the server cannot be reached, nothing changes and a short message says so.

steps.path: Browser panel, on a computer that blocks the browser's extra protection
steps.headline: "Extra protection off" is now the app's normal warning box: one line and a Got it button.
steps.changed: The custom chip is gone. This is the same amber notice box used elsewhere, with the explanation folded under Details.
steps.notice: Small at rest. Got it hides it until you next open YouCoded.
steps.risk: It is a warning box, so it takes a little more room than a chip did.

steps.headline: Details opens inside the box, exactly like other errors with Details.
steps.changed: The explanation and the fix sit in the same Details fold the app's errors use.
steps.notice: The picture below moves down a little while it is open.

steps.path: docs/active/design/2026-10-13-ui-design-guide.md, section "New UI reuses what exists, and stays short"
steps.headline: Replace last round's design guide section with these two rules?
steps.today: Last round's section listed five rules, including a small amber chip, and went further than you asked.
steps.problem: New screens kept arriving with their own styling and too many words.
steps.proposal: Two rules only. (1) Reuse the existing screen and its styling; find one that does the same job, put it beside yours, and build yours from that same piece. (2) Keep copy minimal: one short line, details behind an existing expand or confirm, say a fact once.
steps.risk: Advice to future builders, not an automatic block.
